geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Hinged triangle model: open wider, side grows; then settle the 2.9 shortest-path conjecture.

Goal: I can order sides from angles and angles from sides, and prove the perpendicular is the shortest segment from a point to a line.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
In a triangle, if one side is longer than another, the angle opposite the longer side is larger. Conversely, if one angle is larger than another, the side opposite the larger angle is longer.

So the longest side is opposite the largest angle. Proof idea: if AC > AB, mark D on AC with AD = AB. Triangle ABD is isosceles, so angle ABD = angle ADB, and angle ADB is an exterior angle of triangle BDC, so it is greater than angle C. Then angle ABC > angle ABD = angle ADB > angle C.

Consequence: the perpendicular segment from a point to a line is the shortest one, because in the right triangle the 90 degree angle is the largest (by 5.2, each other angle is less than the 90 degree exterior angle at the right angle), so the slanted segment opposite it is longer.

slides.html: In triangle PQR, angle P = 50, angle Q = 60 and angle R = 70 degrees. Which side is longest?
slides.reveal: PQ, the side opposite the largest angle R.
